result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.schema.ts defines guests as z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refinement, and addGuests.handler.ts's uniqueGuests filter only checks guests against existing booking.attendees (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`) — a case-sensitive comparison with no intra-request dedup. So duplicate emails within one request (or case-variant duplicates) are inserted via createMany, exactly as the finding describes; the Set-based refine exists only in the client dialog.

judged_text: The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client dialog enforces (AddGuestsDialog.tsx refine on Set size), and the handler's filter dedupes only against existing attendees with a case-sensitive comparison, so duplicate guests within one request are accepted. A direct call to trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests with guests ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] (or 'A@b.com' when 'a@b.com' is already an attendee) inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same person and sends duplicate invite emails; only the client-side Set check prevents this for UI users, so any non-UI caller corrupts the attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates email format and does not enforce uniqueness like the client dialog’s local refine. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing `booking.attendees` using case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email` and does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `['a@b.com','a@b.com']` will remain duplicated and be inserted via `createMany`. Case variants (e.g., existing attendee `a@b.com` + request `A@b.com`) also bypass the filter. Since emails are sent based on the resulting attendees list (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` in sendAddGuestsEmails), duplicate attendee rows can cause duplicate emails. Thus non-UI callers can corrupt attendee data and trigger duplicate sends.
